archiveTake: A funny, warm, constantly expanding sci-fi adventure that somehow still feels like home.
spoilerFreeReview: I loved Midnight Burger. It has amazing world-building combined with a cast of characters you really start to love. It starts out small, with a lovable group dashing around the galaxy, but as time goes on our protagonists start running into challenges that test them in every way possible. The world keeps expanding, and every time you think it can't get any bigger, it does. There is always a new world for them to explore and a new challenge for them to face, but through it all, there's a diner.
The character development is really good. The characters grow as people over the course of the show, not because of one pivotal moment, but by slowly learning through challenge and hardship.

It's funny and unserious at times, while at others being intense and surprisingly serious. You don't just feel like you're observing everything from the outside; it often feels like you're right there experiencing it with the characters.
I would absolutely recommend this to someone who wants something easy to get into that gradually drags you in, while still being funny and serious at the same time.
thoughts: What I love most about Midnight Burger is how comfortable it can feel even when everything around the characters is completely insane. No matter how big the story gets or how far they travel, the diner gives the whole show this sense of familiarity.

It is also one of those shows where I ended up caring about the characters way more than I expected. The bigger sci-fi ideas are great, but the reason I keep coming back is the people inside the diner.
